comparator.name: Science for Sustainable Societies
comparator.sourceNotes: Current 2026–2027 BA-SFS catalogue and individual module entries control years 1–2. The new Politics of Sustainability Solutions replaces Responsible Research and Innovation. Systems Modelling and Research Design in Practice are confirmed at 5 and 4 EC respectively. The current programme chart and catalogue groups jointly support the 30 EC open semester, 11 EC Sustainable Societies Project, 18 EC thesis and 1 EC Learning My Way in year three. OER §3.1 requires 45 first-year EC before year-two courses, Mathematics for Sustainability and/or Programming in Python before Systems Modelling, the full first year and 45 year-two EC including Research Design in Practice before the project and thesis, and prior Learning My Way before the next annual unit.
components: Introduction to Science for Sustainable Societies
Earth System Science in the Anthropocene

core: Integrated natural-science understanding of climate, Earth systems, ecology and biodiversity
Social and behavioural analysis of human–environment relationships
Governance, policy and socially effective sustainability transitions
Quantitative, computational, spatial and interdisciplinary research methods
adjacent: Pollution, resource use, industrial ecology and energy transitions
questions: How can spatial evidence and natural-science models guide socially workable climate adaptation?
Which governance and economic choices support fair resource and energy transitions?

trace: Introduces physical and quantitative principles used to examine sustainability systems.
Studies interacting lithosphere and hydrosphere processes through Earth science and field labs.
Introduces incentives, markets and scarcity for evaluating environmental choices.
Applies sustainability analysis to an interdisciplinary real-world case.
Introduces quantitative research design and statistics for economic or environmental evidence.
Analyses natural hazards, exposure, climate-driven risks and adaptation measures.
Supplies calculus and linear algebra for quantitative modelling of systems.
Examines climate drivers, impacts and adaptation, including sea-level rise.
Uses nature-based coastal engineering, flood protection and land-reclamation cases to study adaptation options.
Introduces biodiversity patterns, ecological interactions, threats and conservation as scientific foundations for sustainability.
Works with and visualises spatial datasets as evidence for interdisciplinary inquiry.
Uses GIS, satellite and drone data to investigate environmental change.
Studies soils and aquifers with field and laboratory analysis relevant to water resources and coastal defence.
Analyses choice under scarcity and regulation, grounding economic evaluation of resource use.
Studies flood, sea-level and subsidence adaptation through delta water-management projects.
Models water–rock–soil cycles and resource recovery in a geochemical case.
Examines circular-economy recovery technologies, material stewardship and resource security.
Provides probability and statistical inference for quantitative environmental evidence.
Small teams investigate regionally situated sustainability questions supplied by external organizations, developing research questions, plans and evidence.
Researches geoscience of geothermal energy, waste storage and carbon capture.
Evaluates how government and non-government stakeholders shape sustainability policy.
Develops causal and predictive empirical analysis of economic data; environmental application is a possible project, not course-specific.
Examines environmental justice movements and the social distribution of environmental costs.
Models interactions among Earth spheres with climate proxies and a field trip.
Studies public goods, externalities, taxation and welfare effects of policy, applicable to environmental decisions.
Develops predictive methods for datasets; environmental spatial applications would need a selected project.
Designs lower-carbon energy systems with technical and economic assessment.
Studies ecosystem dynamics, ecological modelling and applied cases.
Examines aggregate economic growth and policy conditions for large-scale energy transitions.
Investigates biases and behavioural incentives that affect resource-use decisions.

alternatives.label: Integrated Sustainability Science
alternatives.concept: Combine Earth systems, climate and ecology with economics, governance and environmental justice. Statistics and spatial data support environmental analysis, and a team project introduces research on a regional sustainability question.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule deliberately spans natural systems, social and economic analysis, policy, quantitative methods and applied sustainability research.
progression: The partner research project is available in the first term and has no formal prerequisite. The later course sequence develops disciplinary and quantitative depth. All formal gateways and offering constraints pass.

alternatives.label: Climate Resilience and Spatial Environmental Data
alternatives.concept: Study climate hazards, soils, groundwater, delta water management and nature-based adaptation. Use spatial observations and machine learning to investigate environmental change, with public economics to assess policy choices.
alternatives.labelReason: The scheduled courses explicitly develop climate risk, water and soils, Earth observation, modelling, data analysis and public choices about adaptation.
progression: The partner research project is available in the first term and has no formal prerequisite. The later course sequence develops disciplinary and quantitative depth. All formal gateways and offering constraints pass.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the integrated route, this schedule adds Earth-system modelling, machine learning, renewable-system design and public economics while dropping advanced mathematics, microeconomics, environmental justice and one governance course. Its organising question is spatial climate resilience.

alternatives.label: Resources, Energy and Sustainability Policy
alternatives.concept: Study resource extraction, material recovery and renewable energy systems alongside economics and governance. Examine how policy and markets shape the use of resources and the costs and benefits of energy transitions.
alternatives.labelReason: Resource geoscience, energy design, economics, governance and behavioural choice form the scheduled focus.
progression: The partner research project is available in the first term and has no formal prerequisite. The later course sequence develops disciplinary and quantitative depth. All formal gateways and offering constraints pass.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces flood-hazard, aquifer and water-management depth with ecosystems, macroeconomic conditions, public economics, energy design and behavioural choices. It therefore changes both the environmental subject and the policy question.

candidates.label: Climate Resilience and Spatial Environmental Data

routeSelection.basis: The official programme has no named track or specialisation to choose. The reconstruction therefore uses every compulsory component and preserves the full 30-EC open third-year space without filling it to improve UCR fit.

selection.assessment: Three evidence-backed UCR programmes are feasible and pairwise distinct by at least four courses: integrated sustainability science; climate resilience with spatial environmental data; and resources, energy and sustainability policy. Remaining interest rows elaborate examples, methods and outcomes rather than a fourth coherent direction.

blocks: Earth systems, ecology, climate and field evidence
Both introduce integrated sustainability questions; the UCR gateway is broader and course-sized.
Both introduce ecology and biodiversity in the context of sustainability.
Both introduce interacting Earth systems and human pressures.
Both address climate change and societal consequences; UCR emphasizes physical and sustainability dimensions.
Both analyse ecosystems and biodiversity; UCR does not reproduce the Leiden livelihoods module.
Both model environmental systems. Leiden focuses on economy–environment interactions, including input-output and material-flow models.
Both develop field-based environmental evidence, though UCR focuses on soils and aquifers.
Both study how environmental costs and benefits are distributed. UCR focuses on social movements and environmental justice, while Leiden takes an anthropological approach.
Both examine relations among science, technology and societal transitions.
Both study actors, institutions and policy choices in sustainability governance.
Leiden applies psychology to environmental behavior.
Leiden combines food-system ecology with food policy and governance.
Leiden studies climate mitigation policy through peatland carbon cases.
Both address pollution, material flows and power; UCR focuses on circular delta systems.
Methods, projects and open programme space
Both support reflection and academic development, but Leiden’s Learning My Way is programme-specific.
Both provide mathematical foundations for quantitative sustainability work.
Both teach social-science research design and statistics.
Both introduce programming and data analysis; UCR is not sustainability-specific.
Both use empirical tools to address economic questions. Leiden applies them specifically to evaluating social and environmental policy.
Both use team inquiry into a problem supplied by an external organization. Leiden’s required consultancy course develops and presents a project plan.
Programme-specific second-year Learning My Way unit.
The genuine 30-EC minor/elective/exchange space remains student-selected and is not a fixed external course to align.
The compulsory independent 18-EC thesis cannot be counted as an ordinary UCR course or UCR’s optional research element.
Programme-specific third-year Learning My Way unit.
Leiden prepares students for the thesis through a dedicated sequence on research questions and design.

notes.text: UCR offers related coursework and a team research project. Leiden combines natural and social science in dedicated modules on food systems, well-being and livelihoods. Its required fieldwork, 11 EC consultancy project and 18 EC thesis are distinctive parts of the degree.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Science for Sustainable Societies degree combines ecology and Earth science with social science, governance and data analysis. Students apply these perspectives to sustainability challenges through fieldwork, a team consultancy project and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers three options emphasizing broad sustainability science, climate adaptation and spatial data, or resources and energy policy. Leiden has a dedicated sequence of co-taught modules, field methods, consultancy and independent research.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC curriculum includes 30 EC of open study, an 11 EC consultancy project and an 18 EC thesis. Entry to the project and thesis requires completing year one and earning 45 EC in year two, including Research Design in Practice.
